title: Model homotopy colimit cocones become localized colimits
statement:
Use simplicial sets and infinity categories in fixed universes [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A combinatorial model category $\mathcal M$ means a complete and cocomplete locally presentable category with weak equivalences $W$ closed under retracts and satisfying two-out-of-three, and classes of cofibrations $C$ and fibrations $F$ such that $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems generated by sets, with functorial factorizations. Locally presentable means generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits, for some regular $\kappa$, by a small set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve these colimits. A weak factorization system is a factorization of every arrow into its left and right classes, each class characterized by diagonal lifting against the other. A cofibrant object has its initial map in $C$. There exists a universal homotopy coherent localization $q:N(\mathcal M)\to\mathcal M[W^{-1}]_\infty$: restriction into any infinity category identifies the functor infinity category out of the target with the full subcategory of functors out of $N(\mathcal M)$ inverting $W$.

For every small ordinary category $I$, the projective model structure on $\mathcal M^I$ exists, with objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations. If $D:I\to\mathcal M$ and $QD\to D$ is a projectively cofibrant replacement, then the ordinary colimit cocone $QD\to\operatorname{colim}_I QD$, after applying $q$ and identifying $qQD$ with $qD$, is a colimit cocone in $\mathcal M[W^{-1}]_\infty$. In particular a model homotopy pushout square, meaning a cocone on a span for which the comparison from the colimit of a projectively cofibrant replacement is a weak equivalence, becomes a pushout square there. This assertion includes the maps of the cocone and its coherent universal property, and does not assume that $\mathcal M$ is simplicial or that the original diagram $D$ is objectwise cofibrant.
